security_privacy_cost_impact: Security: assertion and tooling only; no grant, policy, role or schema changes. Each closure refuses a later migration that weakens an unread guarantee, none reachable by a client on the clean set: a trigger on any app or private table (A1 R-2, the lifecycle_state writer among them), a schema owner or a non-client role attribute changed (A1 S1, S3; Q0 R-2), an index whose collation or operator class does not serve its predicate (Q0 R-2), a COPY ... PROGRAM in a migration (a server shell command, C0 G1), and test-reach gaps in the static suites. Redaction now covers a fragment-carried host (G-2). Cost: the pinned grant probe runs two more drift jobs (eight in all); migrate-clean stays about 5 s of probe time on this host. Review round: a trigger hidden by marking it internal in pg_catalog (A1-OT-1), COPY to or from a server file and the server-file function calls (C0-OT-2, Q0-OT-3), and quoted or commented spellings past 170's do-block allowlist (C0-OT-1) are refused; redaction also covers a percent-encoded user, database and host, a host list and an IPv6 zone id (A1-OT-4). The pinned trigger probe runs one more drift job (three).
migration_and_data_impact: None. No migration file is added or edited. Two lint files change one _how_measured line each (regenerated on the clean set), and the retention and audit coverage maps change only their blocker citations (line numbers to quotes; three retention-map quotes lengthened in the review round so each is said by one blocker only).
compatibility_impact: Tests stay 684 (none added or renamed); foundation-contract's assertion floor 946 -> 1000 -> 1014 (the review round) and identity-isolation's 2167 -> 2169, the guard's own count; rls-smoke cases unchanged at 1087. Probe digests move for the pinned trigger (twice), pinned grant and index coverage probes only. A later batch that adds a migration must regenerate pinned-grants.json and the known exceptions (their _how_measured names the last migration), one that adds a trigger must pin it, and a migration may no longer carry COPY to or from a server file or call a server-file function. The amendment paths stay three, so no open_blockers line pin moves.
known_limitations: The pinned trigger probe reads tables in app and private only; a trigger on a table in another schema, such as a child in public, is read by no rule here (A1-OT-I2, Q0-OT-9).
The export rule's token/credential half reads column NAMES (token, secret, credential, password; a *_redacted flag excepted); a material column named otherwise is the §5 cell's to class.

The audit-table tripwire is a text scan of the spellings its test pins, comments read as whitespace: a dynamic EXECUTE, a function a trigger runs rewritten in place (held by the pinned trigger probe's digest) and any spelling not pinned are not read by it; the live probes hold the catalog, and the catalog assertion for every role on either audit table stays owed with batch 141's migration (open_blockers[191] (9)).

Words or names computed at run time (a COPY, a server-file call or an encoding name built by EXECUTE or a wrapper) are not read by the lexer, as for client_encoding; rls-smoke reads no migration text, so a migration carrying a refused shape is refused by migrate-clean.
The pinned grant probe's rules 7 and 8, like 2-4, fail by design on a provisioned platform instance until Q170-c measures its roles, schema owners and default ACLs.
The grant files' measured-on version is read from the file it checks, and generate-pinned-grants.mjs --check runs in no make target or CI workflow (Q0-OT-6): it is held by a manual --check only.
redactConnection is not libpq's parser: it reads more URL pieces than libpq connects by, never fewer, and leaves a piece of two characters or less unredacted.
